summary: Created T105–T108 as the four P06 successors to T063, T064, T066 and T067, completed their downstream migration accounting, synchronized all live editable ownership/security/traceability collateral, and recorded every affected planned contract plus the final-evidence gate.
rationale: The Owner directed a behavioral replacement, not an in-place rewrite of approved work. The four new contracts retain the predecessors' valid acceptance and safety obligations, add the A0013 registry corrections, preserve historical evidence read-only, and require the old authoritative paths to become unreachable after a fail-closed cutover. The dependency order is acyclic: T105 depends on registry producer T068, so T068 must remove its old reverse dependency on T063 rather than point to T105; T106 then consumes T105, T107 consumes T105/T106, and T108 consumes T105. Existing approved contracts and their evidence remain byte-identical. A0013 legacy impacts remain open here because only the later SUPERSEDE amendment may close them while annotating the exact successors. Attempt 2 also synchronizes the live goal/spec mapping while preserving both predecessor and successor entries until SUPERSEDE, and records T096 separately because the earlier A0013 T096 finding does not cover the new successor evidence. Attempt 3 completes the collateral and contract-reference scan: it adds T087/T088/T102 as exact impacts, records their migration in T105/T106, synchronizes ARCHITECTURE and THREAT_MODEL ownership, updates ADR-003, and marks the delivered T067 guide and the old documentation audit with explicit transition/history boundaries.

impact_assessment.intent: Behavioral replacement implementing the already-confirmed G-STRATEGY-REGISTRY-01 and G-BACKTEST-RUN-01 direction. No Intent text or intent_revision changed: A0014 adds execution tasks for settled requirements and introduces no V2, chain, pool-selection, risk or live-policy choice.
impact_assessment.specification: No product behavior or unresolved choice changed. ARCHITECTURE §2.2 now records both predecessor delivery history and T105–T108 successor ownership with a fail-closed transition rule; THREAT_MODEL T-17/T-21 now names T105/T106 controls, owners and evidence while retaining predecessor history; ADR-003 points current manifest recording to T105 after retirement. Intent and spec_revision remain unchanged because these edits synchronize ownership for requirements already settled by G-STRATEGY-REGISTRY-01 and A0014.
impact_assessment.contracts: Added exactly four new contracts: T105 replaces T063, T106 replaces T064, T107 replaces T066 and T108 replaces T067. No contract that existed before A0014 was edited. Nine existing PLANNED contracts require later CONTRACT amendment: T068, T069, T073, T083, T084, T087, T088, T101 and T102; T096 must include all four successor evidence paths. T087/T088 replace normative T063 references with T105, while T102 directly depends on and cites T106.
impact_assessment.dependencies: The new graph remains acyclic: T105=[T063,T068], T106=[T064,T068,T105], T107=[T065,T066,T068,T105,T106], T108=[T067,T068,T105]. T068 removes T063 without adding T105, avoiding a cycle. T069/T073/T084/T101 replace T063 with T105; T073/T083 replace T066 with T107. T087/T088 consume T105 transitively through the amended T069 but must cite T105 as manifest authority. T102 adds a direct T106 dependency because no existing closure path supplies the current robustness protocol. T096 must include all four successors and depend directly on T108.
impact_assessment.implementation: T105 governs current robinhood_lp.reports publication/rerun, T106 robustness surfaces/runner/reports, T107 experiments lock/search/harness, and T108 the authoring guide/example/tests. Their migration sections now account for T087/T088/T102 and T096. ARCHITECTURE maps the actual successor surfaces. The current T067 guide carries a transition notice that preserves callback mechanics but rejects free-text identity authority; no business implementation or test was changed.
impact_assessment.data: Existing T063/T064/T066 manifests, reports, surfaces, locks, rejected runs, checksums and review artifacts remain byte-for-byte read-only. New artifacts bind registry/schema identity, version and checksum. Missing bindings are explicit legacy state, never inferred or backfilled; any migration is additive, retains the source checksum/provenance and cannot turn prior test-fold exposure into a fresh candidate. T108 has no mutable production data and leaves manifest migration to T105. T087/T088 must resolve current coverage/checksums through T105; T102 must consume T106 schema-bound robustness evidence. Architecture, threat and historical-audit edits do not mutate any runtime artifact.
impact_assessment.operations: Cutover order is T068 registry, T105 manifest, T106 robustness, then T107 candidate lock; T108 can follow T068/T105. Publication/evaluation fails closed on missing or incompatible revisions. Rollback pauses publication/evaluation or restores the last compatible registry-bound release and cannot reactivate hard-coded identity, unrestricted surfaces or old candidate locks. T069 alone owns durable run state, cancellation and restart; rerun-manifest remains an artifact operation unless invoked through a new T069 run record. T087/T088 remain T069-backed product surfaces and cannot make a legacy manifest current; T102 fails closed when T106 evidence is absent/incompatible. The architecture transition rule makes an unapproved successor unavailable after predecessor retirement rather than permitting fallback.
impact_assessment.security: Registry/schema metadata grants no approval, risk, signer, execution or live authority. THREAT_MODEL T-17/T-21 now names T105/T106 as successor controls and keeps T063/T064 only as historical delivery after retirement. T087/T088 remain read/control surfaces over T069 and cannot rewrite provenance; T102 remains unable to bypass central risk. The T067 guide transition notice expressly rejects notes/display text as identity.
impact_assessment.verification: Each successor requires positive, negative, compatibility, migration and old-path-unreachable evidence. T105 adds registered/unregistered, parameter/schema/revision/code and artifact-vs-product-rerun cases; T106 adds range-edge and invalid surface cases; T107 changes every new frozen field and tests tamper/downgrade/one-look behavior; T108 tests registered identity, free-text rejection, runnable example, citations and drift. Existing predecessor acceptance remains required. Independent Developer/Reviewer evidence is still required; this planning amendment itself is not acceptance evidence. T096 must map the independently approved evidence for T105–T108, including T108 guide/example/drift evidence, rather than treating predecessor approval as successor evidence. T087/T088 require current/legacy, mismatch and old-path-unreachable page tests; T102 requires positive schema-bound evaluation plus invalid-schema, legacy-path, migration and fail-closed tests. The collateral rescan covered every Prophet-editable file that names T063/T064/T066/T067 or the replaced modules/artifacts; historical snapshots were marked rather than rewritten.

affected_existing_tasks.reason: T068 currently depends on T063 and says it modifies the T063 manifest path. T105 is now the designated registry-bound manifest successor and depends on T068, so replacing T063 with T105 inside T068 would create a cycle while leaving T063 would strand an ordinary PLANNED consumer on a retired predecessor. The contract must identify T068 as the registry producer and T105 as the downstream integration owner rather than claiming the old manifest as its dependency.
affected_existing_tasks.required_disposition: CONTRACT: revise T068 to preserve registry/schema/provenance delivery while moving current manifest binding and its integration acceptance to T105. DEPENDENCY: remove T063 and do not add T105, because T105 depends on T068. IMPLEMENTATION: T068 may expose deterministic registry validation but must not establish a second manifest publisher; T105 performs cutover from the old validator. DATA: registry records are new and deterministic; historical manifests are handled by T105, not rewritten by T068. OPERATIONS: registry must be available before T105 cutover; missing registry fails closed. SECURITY: unchanged—no RPC/storage/signer/Web import or authority. VERIFICATION: test registry behavior locally and let T105 prove manifest integration and old-path unreachability.

SECURITY: no new permission or secret surface. VERIFICATION: cover new run, linked rerun, cancellation/failure and rejection of legacy/unregistered inputs.

affected_existing_tasks.required_disposition: CONTRACT/DEPENDENCY: replace T063 with T105 and require displayed manifest provenance to include registered identity and schema/registry revision. IMPLEMENTATION: presentation reads T105 artifacts without inventing or rewriting identity. DATA: historical T063 artifacts remain explicitly legacy and read-only.
